scope: Read-only review of the complete fixed TouchTransaction class only. WIP ActionRunner, Android adapter, authority/target selection and UI runtime are outside this review.
conclusion: No new concrete blocker identified in this narrowly declared one-pointer-stream Exception-handling contract.

observations.finding: Each inject site occurs at most once, without retry loops. downAttempted and upAttempted are set immediately before the corresponding inject call, preserving uncertain-attempt state when inject returns false or throws an Exception.

After any attempted DOWN without acknowledged UP, finally attempts to create one CANCEL and invokes its inject at most once. A failed/uncertain DOWN does not advance to UP; an acknowledged UP does not emit a redundant CANCEL. CANCEL failure does not cause a second DOWN, UP or CANCEL.

The class checks nonnegative elapsed time before DOWN admission, before UP creation and again after UP creation. The 150 ms value bounds these observed admissions only; it does not bound a blocking inject call, guarantee actual event delivery time, or provide process-tree cleanup.

Observation.remember preserves the first Exception object as primary and records later cancellation/recycle/final-clock Exceptions in secondary. The normal false-ack paths become explicit Fault errors. Successful cleanup cannot erase a prior pointer-stream failure.

The available up/down/cancel references are each passed once to an independent recycle try/catch. An Exception during one recycle does not skip the other available events, and allCreatedRecycled remains false for a created event whose recycle did not return.

inputTerminated treats an attempted but unacknowledged DOWN/UP without acknowledged CANCEL as unresolved. It is a termination observation, not a complete success predicate; the WIP caller must still account for primary and recycling state.

limitations: No compilation, control run or Android execution by this reviewer. The reported 16 host controls use explicit backend/time/allocation seams and are not independently rerun here.
Java Error subclasses, OOM during observation allocation, hard kill and permanently blocked Binder/backend calls are not covered by this Exception-only completion contract.

The Backend contract must provide the intended distinct owned event objects and must not inject unrelated input inside obtain, beforeDown, recycle or now; the Android implementation of that contract was not reviewed.
No claim about the enclosing helper authority, package/window/coordinate validation, input permissions, root/Main lifecycle or whole-app readiness.
publication_owner: Android CP15; do not duplicate this review in Native source catalog.
